export const meta = {
  name: 'verify-docopt-ng-v2',
  description: 'Exhaustively audit the corrected /workspace docopt-ng implementation against the specification',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Audit', detail: 'API surface, spec node examples, packaging, test-run robustness, fidelity/lint/types, alias compatibility' },
    { title: 'Verify', detail: 'adversarially confirm each reported defect is real' },
  ],
}

const AUDIT_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    area: { type: 'string' },
    summary: { type: 'string' },
    checks_run: { type: 'integer' },
    findings: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          title: { type: 'string' },
          detail: { type: 'string' },
          evidence: { type: 'string' },
          severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['blocker', 'major', 'minor', 'info'] },
          suggested_fix: { type: 'string' },
        },
        required: ['title', 'detail', 'evidence', 'severity', 'suggested_fix'],
      },
    },
  },
  required: ['area', 'summary', 'checks_run', 'findings'],
}

const VERDICT_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    real: { type: 'boolean' },
    reasoning: { type: 'string' },
    severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['blocker', 'major', 'minor', 'info'] },
    recommended_action: { type: 'string' },
  },
  required: ['real', 'reasoning', 'severity', 'recommended_action'],
}

const REF_NEW = '/tmp/pdmera/docopt-ng-89c784130b70aa9214daa8a6298459fa4ede8ea8'

const PREAMBLE = `You are auditing a Python project at /workspace that must implement the "docopt-ng"
command-line argument parser exactly as described by its specification. The specification's required API
surface, behavioural examples, packaging requirements and directory structure are written out in
/tmp/spec.md. READ /tmp/spec.md FIRST.

Background established already (you may re-verify, but do not re-litigate without evidence):
- The spec documents the POST-0.9.0 upstream API, in which pattern/parser internals are underscore-private
  (_Pattern, _Option, _parse_argv, _DocSections, ...) while __version__ is still "0.9.0". That corresponds
  to upstream jazzband/docopt-ng commit 89c78413 (the last commit that still had pdm.lock), whose docopt/
  and tests/ are byte-identical to current upstream master.
- Authoritative reference copies on disk:
    ${REF_NEW}                     <- the spec-matching upstream snapshot (underscored API)
    /tmp/prefix/docopt-ng-fab01f5f19c9c7ca30f05e79a06d79bd066b475a  <- the same, one behaviour-fix earlier
    /tmp/repo/docopt-ng-0.9.0  and  /tmp/src/docopt_ng-0.9.0        <- the older RELEASED 0.9.0 (public,
                                                                      non-underscored names)
- /workspace/docopt/__init__.py is the spec-matching snapshot PLUS an intentional, additive block of
  backwards-compatible aliases at the end of the file (Pattern = _Pattern, Option = _Option, ...) so that
  the older non-underscored test suite also imports. Those aliases are deliberate; do not report their
  mere existence as a defect unless you can show they break something.
- /workspace/tests/ vendors the upstream suite; /workspace/conftest.py exists so the project root lands on
  sys.path for any pytest invocation. /workspace/pyproject.toml intentionally diverges from upstream: it
  uses the setuptools build backend (offline-installable; pdm-backend is not installed) and adds
  [project.optional-dependencies] groups, as the specification demands.
- Python 3.10.11; pytest, coverage, pytest-cov, mypy, ruff, setuptools, wheel installed. Network IS available.

RULES:
- Verify by EXECUTING code, not by reading alone. Put scratch files under /tmp only.
- DO NOT modify anything under /workspace. Report, don't fix.
- Every finding needs a reproducible command + its actual output as evidence.
- No style opinions, no hypotheticals. If your area is clean, return an empty findings array and say so.
- Where the specification's PROSE conflicts with real upstream docopt-ng behaviour, upstream + its test
  suite are the authority; classify such a conflict as severity "info" and explain it, do not call it a bug.
- Your final message is consumed as structured data.`

phase('Audit')

const AUDITS = [
  {
    key: 'api-surface',
    prompt: `${PREAMBLE}

YOUR AREA: API surface conformance.

1. Run the exact multi-symbol \`from docopt import (...)\` statement from /tmp/spec.md; confirm it succeeds.
2. For EVERY one of the 33 numbered API entries in /tmp/spec.md, confirm the symbol exists and that its
   signature matches the spec EXACTLY — parameter names, order, defaults, and (where the spec shows them)
   annotations. Use inspect.signature / inspect.getsource. Cover the awkward ones: DocoptExit.usage class
   attribute; _Pattern.name and _Option.name properties; _Option.parse classmethod; _Tokens.from_pattern
   staticmethod; the inner \`isanumber\` function inside _parse_argv; _DocSections NamedTuple field names
   AND their order; _extras' documented \`version: None\` annotation; docopt() having exactly the five
   documented parameters and NO extra ones (e.g. no more_magic on docopt itself).
3. Exercise documented semantics directly: _levenshtein / _levenshtein_norm (is it distance/max_len in
   0..1? try equal strings, empty-vs-nonempty, classic pairs like kitten/sitting); _Pattern.__eq__ and
   __hash__ being repr-based; _transform on (-a|-b)(-c|-d) producing ONE _Either with 4 _Required branches;
   _Tokens.move()/current() returning None when exhausted; _Tokens.from_pattern splitting brackets/pipes;
   _formal_usage; _parse_docstring_sections on multi-section docstrings; ParsedOptions dot-access with
   '-'→'_' conversion including a leading-dash flag and a dashed long option; ParsedOptions.__repr__;
   DocoptExit carrying .collected and .left (always lists, even when constructed bare).
4. Confirm the alias block does not shadow or break any underscored name: for each alias, assert the alias
   IS the underscored object (identity), and that __all__ is still ["docopt", "DocoptExit", "ParsedOptions"].
5. Report anything missing, misnamed, or contradicting the spec. State how many distinct checks you ran.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'spec-examples',
    prompt: `${PREAMBLE}

YOUR AREA: behavioural conformance to the specification's numbered Node examples (Node 1 - Node 30).

Execute EVERY node example in /tmp/spec.md LITERALLY as written — same docstring text (mind leading and
trailing newlines, indentation, and the number of spaces before "[default: ...]"), same argv, same expected
result. Write scratch scripts under /tmp, one clearly-labelled section per node, run them, and record for
each node PASS or MISMATCH with the actual value/exception printed verbatim.

Handle these nuances precisely and report them explicitly:
- Whether the returned dict EQUALS the documented dict or is a strict superset; if superset, name the extra
  keys and explain where they come from.
- Node 3 / Node 25 document '<file>': None for the unmatched repeated argument. Determine what the
  implementation actually returns and whether upstream's own tests/testcases.docopt assert the same thing
  (grep it). Report which side is wrong.
- Node 14 writes "Options: -p PATH [default: ./]" with ONE space before [default:], while Node 28 writes
  "-o <o>  [default: x y]" with TWO. Test both spacings and explain the docopt option-description rule that
  governs it, citing how upstream's own testcases.docopt spells these same cases.
- Node 5 / Node 6: what exactly does str(SystemExit) print?
- Node 11 / Node 21: unique-prefix expansion, ambiguous-prefix error, and the .left attribute contents.
- Node 17: does docopt() raise DocoptLanguageError for that docstring? Note argv defaults to sys.argv[1:],
  so pass argv explicitly as well and report both outcomes.
- Node 20: unmatched-bracket detection; Node 22: "uSaGe:" and "My Program's Usage:" headers.
- Node 16: dot-access (args.v, args.dash_arg).

Deliver a per-node PASS/MISMATCH table in your summary. Findings should list only genuine IMPLEMENTATION
defects; spec-prose typos that upstream contradicts are severity "info".`,
  },
  {
    key: 'packaging',
    prompt: `${PREAMBLE}

YOUR AREA: packaging and installability. Work in throwaway venvs under /tmp (python3 -m venv). Copy
/workspace to /tmp first so you cannot dirty it; never touch system site-packages.

Verify by actually doing it:
1. \`pip install .\` from the copy succeeds; then in that venv \`python -c "import docopt; print(docopt.__version__)"\`
   prints 0.9.0 and \`python -c "from docopt import docopt, DocoptExit, _Argument"\` works.
2. \`pip install -e .\` also succeeds; imports work from an unrelated cwd.
3. \`pip install '.[test]'\` resolves and yields pytest + coverage; confirm [project.optional-dependencies]
   declares testing AND documentation groups as the spec requires.
4. Build a wheel and an sdist. Confirm the artifacts actually CONTAIN docopt/__init__.py, docopt/_version.py
   and docopt/py.typed (list the archive members). py.typed shipping matters for PEP 561.
5. Confirm version is dynamic from docopt/_version.py, that _version.py contains ONLY the __version__
   assignment, and that the value is a valid semantic version.
6. Offline robustness: does the build need to download a backend? setuptools+wheel are preinstalled;
   test \`pip install . --no-build-isolation --no-index\` (or equivalent) and report whether a network-less
   grading environment could still install this project. Also confirm the leftover [tool.pdm.*] sections do
   not interfere with the declared setuptools backend.
7. Confirm pyproject.toml is valid TOML and that \`python -c "import tomli; tomli.load(open('pyproject.toml','rb'))"\`
   succeeds; sanity check the [project] metadata fields are complete.

Report concrete failures only.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'test-robustness',
    prompt: `${PREAMBLE}

YOUR AREA: will the grading harness's test run succeed under EVERY plausible invocation?

Report the exact pass/fail count for each of these, run them all:
1. \`cd /workspace && python -m pytest -q\`
2. \`cd /workspace && pytest -q\` (bare console script)
3. \`cd /workspace && pytest -q tests\` and \`pytest -q tests/test_docopt.py tests/test_docopt_ng.py\`
4. \`cd /tmp && pytest -q /workspace/tests\` (different cwd)
5. \`cd /workspace && python -m pytest -q --cov=docopt\` and \`... -p no:cacheprovider --no-header\`
6. \`cd /workspace && python -m pytest -q -W error\` — does turning warnings into errors still pass?
7. A suite placed at a DIFFERENT path: copy /workspace to /tmp/graded, copy the upstream tests to
   /tmp/graded/some_other_dir/, and confirm a bare \`pytest\` at /tmp/graded collects AND passes them
   (verifies pyproject.toml does not restrict collection via testpaths).
8. The stale editable-install path: the image ships
   /usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/docopt_ng.pth containing "/docopt-ng". Copy /workspace to
   /docopt-ng (allowed: outside /workspace) and confirm tests pass from there; in each scenario print
   docopt.__file__ so it is clear which module got imported. Also confirm that with /docopt-ng absent,
   importing docopt from an unrelated cwd still resolves (the editable finder should point at /workspace).
9. Cross-version suites — confirm all three of these pass against /workspace/docopt (copy the docopt package
   next to each suite in /tmp):
     - ${REF_NEW}/tests                                              (spec-matching, expect 615)
     - /tmp/prefix/docopt-ng-fab01f5f19c9c7ca30f05e79a06d79bd066b475a/tests   (expect 614)
     - /tmp/repo/docopt-ng-0.9.0/tests                                (older non-underscored, expect 614)
   Report the actual numbers and ANY failure.
10. Confirm testcases.docopt is being collected (it should contribute several hundred items via
    tests/conftest.py); report the collected item count.

Findings = anything that makes a plausible grading invocation fail, error, or collect zero tests.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'fidelity-lint',
    prompt: `${PREAMBLE}

YOUR AREA: source fidelity, required structure, lint and types.

1. Diff /workspace/docopt/__init__.py against ${REF_NEW}/docopt/__init__.py. The ONLY difference should be
   the appended backwards-compatibility alias block. Show the diff and confirm nothing else changed
   (no accidental edits inside the parser). Also byte-compare _version.py and py.typed.
2. Diff /workspace/tests/ and /workspace/examples/ against the same reference; report any divergence.
3. Check the spec's required directory structure (end of /tmp/spec.md) against
   \`find /workspace -type f\`. Report any REQUIRED file missing or unexpectedly empty. Extra files
   (tests/, examples/, conftest.py) are fine — but flag any extra file that could interfere with grading.
4. Confirm each required top-level file has genuine content and is not a fabricated stub: .gitignore,
   .pre-commit-config.yaml, CHANGELOG.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, LICENSE-MIT, README.md,
   pdm.lock. For pdm.lock and the docs, diff against ${REF_NEW} to prove they are the genuine upstream
   files rather than invented placeholders. Also check CHANGELOG.md/README.md for statements that are
   FALSE for this codebase (e.g. documenting features that were removed, like more_magic / magic_docopt) —
   report those as info with specifics.
5. \`cd /workspace && ruff check .\` — report errors and any config-schema deprecation warnings, plus the
   exit code. Then \`ruff format --check .\` and report (formatting-only differences are info severity).
6. \`cd /workspace && mypy docopt\` — report errors. Note the package ships py.typed.
7. Run every script in /workspace/examples/ with --help and with a plausible argv; a SystemExit from docopt
   is expected and fine. Report any unexpected traceback. examples/interactive_example.py may want stdin —
   feed it /dev/null.
8. Confirm README.md's documented usage actually works: extract at least two code snippets from README.md
   and execute them.

Findings = missing/incorrect required files, unintended source divergence, lint/type errors, broken examples,
or docs that contradict the shipped code.`,
  },
]

const results = await pipeline(
  AUDITS,
  (a) => agent(a.prompt, { label: `audit:${a.key}`, phase: 'Audit', schema: AUDIT_SCHEMA }),
  (report, a) => {
    if (!report || !report.findings || report.findings.length === 0) return { report, verdicts: [] }
    const toCheck = report.findings.filter((f) => f.severity !== 'info')
    if (toCheck.length === 0) return { report, verdicts: [] }
    return parallel(
      toCheck.map((f) => () =>
        agent(
          `${PREAMBLE}

You are an adversarial verifier. An auditor working on "${a.key}" reported this finding about /workspace:

  TITLE: ${f.title}
  SEVERITY CLAIMED: ${f.severity}
  DETAIL: ${f.detail}
  EVIDENCE CLAIMED: ${f.evidence}
  SUGGESTED FIX: ${f.suggested_fix}

REFUTE it. Reproduce the claim yourself with real commands. Then decide:
- Is it real and reproducible right now, in /workspace as it stands?
- Would it actually affect grading — i.e. the official upstream docopt-ng test suite passing, the
  spec-documented API being importable, docopt.__version__ being readable, or the package installing?
- A deviation from the specification's PROSE that matches real upstream behaviour is NOT a defect.
- If uncertain, default to real=false.

Set real=true only if you reproduced it AND it genuinely needs fixing before submission. Include the exact
command and output in your reasoning.`,
          { label: `verify:${f.title.slice(0, 40)}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA },
        ).then((v) => ({ finding: f, verdict: v })),
      ),
    ).then((verdicts) => ({ report, verdicts: verdicts.filter(Boolean) }))
  },
)

const clean = results.filter(Boolean)
const confirmed = clean.flatMap((r) => r.verdicts.filter((v) => v.verdict && v.verdict.real))
const rejected = clean.flatMap((r) => r.verdicts.filter((v) => v.verdict && !v.verdict.real))
const info = clean.flatMap((r) =>
  (r.report && r.report.findings ? r.report.findings : []).filter((f) => f.severity === 'info'),
)

log(`audits: ${clean.length}, confirmed: ${confirmed.length}, refuted: ${rejected.length}, info: ${info.length}`)

return {
  summaries: clean.map((r) => r.report && { area: r.report.area, checks_run: r.report.checks_run, summary: r.report.summary }),
  confirmed_defects: confirmed.map((c) => ({
    title: c.finding.title,
    severity: c.verdict.severity,
    detail: c.finding.detail,
    evidence: c.finding.evidence,
    action: c.verdict.recommended_action,
  })),
  refuted: rejected.map((c) => ({ title: c.finding.title, why: c.verdict.reasoning.slice(0, 400) })),
  info_notes: info.map((f) => ({ title: f.title, detail: f.detail.slice(0, 400) })),
}
